title: Marker-Directed State Rewind
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean input word, $B$ a four-tape configuration, and $q,q'$ interpreter controls. Let the state tape $sigma:\mathbb{Z}\to\{0,1,\mathrm{blank}\}$ satisfy $sigma(0)=0$ and $sigma(j)\ne0$ for every positive natural number $j$. Suppose that in control $q$, reading $0$ on work tape $1$ causes a transition to $q'$ with a one-cell right state-head move, while any other read causes the machine to remain in $q$ with a one-cell left move. Then, for every $j\in\mathbb{N}$, from the interpreter configuration with state head at $j$, after $j+1$ steps the control is $q'$ and the state head is at $1$.
hypotheses_covered: specified transition on every non-marker read
replaced:
Suppose the state tape holds the marker symbol $0$ at cell $0$ and no cell at
a positive position holds $0$, and suppose the current control of the stopped
table interpreter moves the state head left on every non-marker read while, on
reading the marker, it moves right once and transfers to a designated
continuation control $q'$.  Then from state cursor $j \in \mathbb{N}$ the
interpreter reaches $q'$ with state cursor $1$ in exactly $j+1$ steps, without
changing any tape contents, the input head, or the output; the premise is
independent of whether the traversed cells are erased blanks or retained unary
symbols.
